    fn service_json(&self) -> String;                          // `ubus call service list '{"name":"dnsmasq"}'`
    fn send_hup(&self, pid: u32);                              // libc::kill(pid, SIGHUP), log on error
}
struct RealSys;
fn converge<S: Sys>(sys: &S, managed_file: &str) -> Result<ConvergeOutcome>;
enum ConvergeOutcome { Ready, DnsmasqStopped }  // Stopped = configured but service intentionally down

Converge algorithm (implement exactly this order): 1. Targeted reverts: uci_revert_option for dhcp.@dnsmasq[0].noresolv, .server, .resolvfile (clears legacy ≤1.31 scheme and our own stale delta; user's other staged dhcp edits untouched). 2. Committed repair: if committed_has_managed_path(sys.committed_dhcp()) → sys.repair_committed_resolvfile() + tracing::warn! (LuCI Save&Apply persisted our staged delta; deleting the option restores stock-default behavior). 3. sys.uci_set("dhcp.@dnsmasq[0].resolvfile", managed_file)? (staged, never committed → reboot auto-reverts). 4. Section discovery: sys.dnsmasq_section(); None → error (NoDnsmasq). 5. If sys.extract… / service_json shows no running instance for the section → log warn!("dnsmasq is not running; leaving it stopped"), return DnsmasqStopped (do NOT start it). 6. If generated_conf(section) already generated_conf_points_at(managed) → return Ready without restart (kills the watchdog-crashloop restart storm). 7. Else sys.restart_dnsmasq()?, then re-read generated_conf and assert it points at managed; on mismatch retry steps 3–7 once (third-party restart raced us), then error loudly (this is the DNS-leak race guard).

    #[derive(Default)]
    struct FakeSys {
        calls: Mutex<Vec<String>>,
        committed: String,
        section: Option<String>,
        // queue of generated-conf reads, popped front on each generated_conf()
        generated: Mutex<Vec<Option<String>>>,
        running: bool,
    }
    impl Sys for FakeSys {
        fn uci_revert_option(&self, key: &str) { self.calls.lock().unwrap().push(format!("revert {key}")); }
        fn uci_set(&self, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<()> {
            self.calls.lock().unwrap().push(format!("set {key}={value}")); Ok(())
        }
        fn repair_committed_resolvfile(&self) -> Result<()> {
            self.calls.lock().unwrap().push("repair-commit".into()); Ok(())
        }
        fn committed_dhcp(&self) -> String { self.committed.clone() }
        fn dnsmasq_section(&self) -> Option<String> { self.section.clone() }
        fn generated_conf(&self, _s: &str) -> Option<String> {
            let mut q = self.generated.lock().unwrap();
            if q.is_empty() { None } else { q.remove(0) }
        }
        fn restart_dnsmasq(&self) -> Result<()> { self.calls.lock().unwrap().push("restart".into()); Ok(()) }
        fn service_json(&self) -> String {
            if self.running {
                r#"{"dnsmasq":{"instances":{"cfg01411c":{"running":true,"pid":42}}}}"#.into()
            } else { r#"{"dnsmasq":{"instances":{}}}"#.into() }
        }
        fn send_hup(&self, pid: u32) { self.calls.lock().unwrap().push(format!("hup {pid}")); }

            ..Default::default()

pub struct Dnsmasq { tx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<Cmd> }   // thin client, one per connect (cheap)
impl Dnsmasq {
    pub fn new() -> Result<Self>;                       // OpenWrt+uci detection, get-or-spawn global actor
    pub async fn set_dns(&mut self, servers: &[IpAddr]) -> Result<()>;
    pub async fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
}
enum Cmd {
    SetTunnel(Vec<IpAddr>, tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<()>>),
    SetWanMirror(tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<()>>),
}
enum Mode { Tunnel, WanMirror }
async fn run_actor<S: Sys>(sys: S, paths: Paths, rx: mpsc::Receiver<Cmd>);  // paths injectable for tests
struct Paths { managed: PathBuf, tmp: PathBuf, wan: PathBuf }

Actor semantics (the review's condition 1 — single writer by construction): - On spawn: run converge (retry lazily on first command if it failed); seed managed file from wan (missing → header-only file); Mode::WanMirror. - SetTunnel: write_managed(render_resolv_conf(&prefer_ipv4_upstreams(servers))) via temp+rename → re-assert generated_conf_points_at (cheap self-heal; on mismatch re-run converge — catches third-party restarts that raced a stale config in) → HUP (cache flush, best-effort, failure = warn not error) → Mode::Tunnel → ack. Log info!("Configured dnsmasq with VPN DNS servers: {:?}") (benchmark marker). - SetWanMirror: copy wan contents (missing → header-only) via temp+rename → HUP → Mode::WanMirror → ack. - 5s tokio::time::interval tick: only in Mode::WanMirror, read wan, compare with current managed content, rename-write only if different, NO HUP (cache flush on background mirror would churn LAN caches). A tick arriving in Mode::Tunnel does nothing — the TOCTOU leak path is structurally impossible because ticks and commands are serialized in one select! loop. - Actor is global: static ACTOR: OnceLock<mpsc::Sender<Cmd>>; Dnsmasq::new() keeps the existing /etc/openwrt_release + uci get dhcp.@dnsmasq[0] detection, then get_or_init spawns run_actor(RealSys, real_paths(), rx) via tokio::spawn (callers are inside the daemon runtime). - Delete from the old implementation: BACKUP_MARKER, RESOLV_CONF/RESOLV_CONF_BACKUP + write_resolv_conf/save_backup/do_reset (conditions 3 & 6: converge IS recovery; the init script's localuse=0 branch points /tmp/resolv.conf at 127.0.0.1 so local programs ride dnsmasq — do not fight it), uci_revert("dhcp") wholesale, unconditional restart_dnsmasq on set/reset, uci_add_list/uci_delete server-list plumbing.

docs.title: Handshake-armed connection probing
docs.text: Date: 2026-07-19 Status: approved

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Time-to-Connected on the router is ~11 s. Benchmarks on the AX1800 (three disconnect→connect cycles, phase boundaries from daemon log timestamps) break it down as:

Phase Run 1 (stale cache) Run 2 (warm) Run 3 (warm) Resolve API addresses 0.14 s 0.12 s ~0.1 s Await account readiness ~0 s ~0 s ~0 s Refresh + select gateways 0.50 s 0.07 s 0.07 s Register with gateways (LP) 1.69 s 1.85 s 1.67 s Tunnel up → viable 8.82 s 8.67 s 8.68 s Total (nym-vpnc connect -w) 11.15 s 10.85 s ~10.6 s

The dominant phase is the viability gate: "Connected" is only declared when the connection monitor's first ICMP probe (single ping to 1.1.1.1 through the exit tunnel) succeeds. The monitor keeps one probe in flight and retransmits at last_sent + timeout; with TimingConfig::two_hop()'s 3 s initial timeout the probes fire at t=0, 3, 6, 9… — so time-to-Connected quantizes to a 3-second grid, and probes sent before the two-hop WireGuard handshakes complete are simply lost. The ~8.7 s constant across runs (with and without a logged handshake retry) is this cadence artifact, not network variance.

Gateway selection is NOT the bottleneck (0.07–0.5 s); upstream's gateway_provider pre-selection work is out of scope here.

docs.title: Prior art
docs.text:
Upstream #5571 (68b638072, still live at their HEAD) solves exactly this for wireguard-go: expose per-peer last_handshake_time from the WG stack via a shareable stats reader, then in tunnel_monitor.rs call wait_for_exit_handshake() — poll every 500 ms, cap at 10 s, never fatal — after the InterfaceUp event is acknowledged and before spawning the connection monitor. The first probe then fires when the tunnel can actually carry it.

Our fork uses gotatun, which makes the port easier than upstream had it: device.read(async |d| d.peers().await) returns Vec<PeerStats> with last_handshake: Option<Duration>. No FFI handle-sharing workarounds needed. Only our nym-wg-gotatun wrapper fails to surface it today.

(Implementation correction: Device derives Clone but the bound requires the transport tuple to be Clone, which our UDP factories are not — so the built design shares an Arc<tokio::sync::RwLock<Option<Device>>> slot between Tunnel and StatsReader instead of cloning Device; stop() takes the slot, readers treat a stopped device as "not handshaken".)

docs.text: On openwrt25, raise logging (nym_connection_monitor=trace plus gotatun handshake logs), run 3 connect cycles, and record per-probe send/reply timestamps and entry/exit handshake completion times. This produces the before-numbers and pins down where inside the 8.7 s the handshake actually lands, so the after-benchmark can attribute any residual gap (e.g. gotatun's 5 s REKEY_TIMEOUT first-handshake retry) correctly.

• New StatsReader struct holding a clone of gotatun::device::Device.
  • Tunnel::stats_reader() returns one.
  • StatsReader::all_peers_have_handshake() -> bool implemented as device.read(async |d| d.peers().await), true iff every peer has last_handshake.is_some().
  • Applies to whichever tunnel variant the two-hop exit actually uses (wireguard_go.rs, and amnezia.rs if trivially symmetric — confirm during implementation).

docs.text: Before the exit tunnel moves into the event-handler task, take exit_tunnel.stats_reader() and store it in TunnelHandle (currently just shutdown token + join handle). Add TunnelHandle::exit_handshake_complete() delegating to the reader. Mixnet tunnels unaffected — the wait is WG-only, guarded the same way as upstream's as_wireguard().

docs.title: Component 3 — tunnel_monitor.rs: the wait
docs.text: Port wait_for_exit_handshake() in shape: poll every 500 ms, cap at 10 s, cancel-safe via the shutdown token, never fatal — on timeout, log and fall through to probing exactly as today. Call site: immediately after the InterfaceUp reply (firewall/routes ready), before create_tunnel_connection_monitor. Probe timings (two_hop()) stay untouched.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Stats-read failures are treated as "not yet handshaken" and polling continues until the cap. Worst case is identical to today's behavior plus at most the 10 s cap, and only in the pathological case where the handshake never completes — where today's probes were all failing anyway on their way to Failed.
